---
title: "About this course"
---

## Who this is for

Students and early-career researchers in health, biology, and data science who want hands-on practice connecting **clinical and public-health questions** to **statistical and machine-learning methods**.

## What you will learn

- How to frame a health research question in a way a model can answer.
- How to find, inspect, and responsibly use open health datasets.
- How to fit, evaluate, and interpret a range of models: regression, trees, boosting, SVMs, clustering, survival, time series, NLP, deep learning, and anomaly detection.
- How to use AI assistants to explain code, suggest diagnostics, and explore alternatives — while keeping yourself in charge of the analysis.

## How the lessons are structured

Each lesson has four parts:

1. **Introduction to the Domain** — background and why the problem matters.
2. **Research Question** — a precise, testable question.
3. **Open-Source Dataset** — a public data source with discussion and a link.
4. **Practical Exercise** — the model/framework to explore, starter code, AI prompts, and extension ideas.

## A note on responsible ML in health

These exercises are **educational**. Health models can harm real people if misused. Always:

- Validate on held-out and, ideally, external data.
- Examine performance across subgroups (fairness).
- Involve clinicians and domain experts.
- Never deploy a model for patient care without proper regulatory and ethical review.
